subject: Set ticks independently for each axis?

messages.author: 40f327279f5af749
messages.subject: Set ticks independently for each axis?
parts:
I guess this is a feature request:

It would be nice to be able to set the ticks independently for each
axis. Since the axis.text and axis.title are independent for each
axis, why not the ticks as well? And while we're at it, how about the
axis.line also? In general, why not make each axis seperately
customizable?

I realize there may be a "consistency" argument to generally want to
avoid this, but there are cases, particularly when using grid.layout
to place multiple graphs on a page, where indepedent control of the
axes would be mighty handy.

Thanks,
AdamK

messages.author: 445326394b5cd0f9
messages.subject: Re: Set ticks independently for each axis?
parts:
In adition to setting ticks independently for each axis, it would be
nice to be able to be able to specify irregularly-spaced points for
tick marks. Yesterday wanted to plot observations at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24,
36, 48, 60, and 72 months. I was happy with the standard gridlines,
but I wanted to have ticks & labels at the points where I had data
(especially since some timepoints are missing from some graphs). So
far as I can tell, in all of R (or S) the only way to do this would be
to print the labels and tick marks as calls to very low level
functions (place text here, know exactly where "here" is, etc.). It
would be sweet if xaxp or something allowed the user to specify a
vector of tick locations for cases like this.

Patrick

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Set ticks independently for each axis?
parts:
You can do this by specifying breaks in scale_x_continuous or
scale_y_continuous.

Hadley
